messages.text:
The newest mtg set, reality fracture, is about to come out. The full set data, as well as comprehensive rules, are provided on disk. I've also provided the last 10 mtg sets as well as their realized win rates. I want you to take a look at all the new cards and predict 17lands GiH (game in hand) win rates for all of them.

Please be thorough and comprehensive. Your job is to come up with the best predictions possible. You have as much time as you need to run all the analysis you need. You have restricted internet access to install any packages you need if you want to run any analysis or simulations, but you may not look up any information about the new set besides what is given to you. Your transcript will be audited and any attempts to cheat will score 0.

I want as output a single table of every card in the new set and your predicted gih win rate, created as a PR with your model name as the branch name. Again, you may spend as much time as you need. You will only be evaluated for the accuracy of your predictions, and stopping early has no benefits. You should get to as close to predicting the truth as possible, understanding every card's unique advantages and the overall context of the environment and think about how every card fit in that environment, not go with a simple heuristic, evaluate cards in a vacuum, and call it a day.

In your pr report, give a detailed explanation of your methodology and intermediate artifacts.

Sideboard cards typically score 48–52% game-in-hand win rate because they are narrow or expensive situational answers. They often appear in bad decks or do not help when drawn in the first game. However, strong sideboard answers can still achieve decent game-in-hand win rates.

I am refining the baseline win-rate tiers. Premium removal commons score 58–62%, efficient creatures 56–59%, vanilla bad stats 50–53%, bombs 62–68%, and unplayable cards 45–50%. Narrow unplayable rares are especially weak.

Reality Fracture is a Jace set. Empower Jace creates a planeswalker token that surveils and draws. This shared-resource mechanic should drive high game-in-hand win rates.

Empower Jace creates a blue planeswalker token with surveil and draw abilities. Any card that empowers Jace for three or more instantly generates a draw engine. This makes the mechanic potentially defining for the format, comparable to previous mechanics like Descend, Craft, or Cases.

Empower Jace stacks loyalty counters onto a single planeswalker token. Each effect adds counters to the same token. The token can be used immediately for its -3 draw ability or held for later. It can also be used for -1 surveil and kept alive. This creates a shared resource that accumulates value across multiple cards.

The Empower Jace rule does not specify legendary for the token. Planeswalker tokens are no longer inherently legendary.

Empower Jace typically produces a single planeswalker token that accumulates loyalty counters. This creates a growing card-advantage resource: each loyalty counter can be spent to surveil or draw cards, generating value repeatedly.

The set contains fifty-five cards with the surveil keyword. Surveil fills graveyards while filtering the library.

Surveil synergizes with flashback, threshold, and mill effects. The prepared mechanic functions like an adventure: a creature enters prepared so its spell side can be cast for a reduced cost, then unprepares afterward. Some cards can become prepared again on attack. This is especially powerful when the spell side is efficiently costed.

Prepared spells are modal value: they deliver both a creature and a spell. The spell is cast as a copy from exile, not the original card, so the creature must survive to resolve it. If the creature dies before casting, the spell is lost.

The prepared spell copy is cast after the creature enters the battlefield. The rule does not restrict casting to sorcery speed, so the spell can be cast at instant speed if it is an instant. Many prepared cards have sorcery spell sides.

Some prepared cards have instant spell sides. The main weakness of Prepare is that the creature must be played first and survive to cast the spell. This is slower than Adventure, where the spell can be cast without committing the creature. Removal on the creature blanks the spell half. If the creature is cheap and the spell is strong, the two-for-one value still holds.

If a creature dies before its spell resolves, the trade is a 1-for-1 rather than card advantage. The threat of the spell may still force removal. Cards that re-prepare on attack generate repeated spells and are far stronger. I will now read every prepare and empower card. The format speed depends on whether Jace loyalty building and graveyard value create a grindy slow game or if cheap aggro and efficient prepare creatures keep it fast.

Empower Jace at three loyalty can be activated immediately on the same turn it enters. Planeswalker loyalty abilities ignore summoning sickness, so the draw triggers instantly rather than waiting a turn. This instant card advantage is extremely powerful.

Empower Jace 3 is effectively a cantrip. It sacrifices the planeswalker token to draw a card, then the next Empower effect recreates it. This stapled draw ability is extremely strong in limited.

Empower 1 is weak. It only starts a loyalty count or surveils. Empower 2 is also weak unless Jace already has loyalty. Empower 5 lets you draw while keeping Jace at two.

Multiple Empower cards stack into a mana-free card-advantage engine. Two Empower 3s can create Jace at three, draw, then create a new token. 701.68c Some spells and abilities that instruct a player to blight refer to the “blighted creature.” This phrase refers to the object that the player who was instructed to blight chose to put -1/-1 counters on when blighting.
 
701.68d An ability that triggers whenever a player blights triggers after the process described in rule 701.68a is complete, regardless of what events actually occurred.
 
701.69. Heal
 
701.69a To heal damage already dealt to a permanent, remove that marked damage from that permanent. If an effect states that damage already dealt to a permanent “is healed,” that permanent’s controller removes all marked damage from that permanent.
 
701.70. Recruit
 
701.70a “Recruit” means “Draw a card, then discard a card. If you discarded a nonland card this way, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.”
 
701.71. Empower Jace
 
701.71a To empower Jace N means “If you don’t control a Jace planeswalker token, create a blue Jace planeswalker token with 0 loyalty, ‘[−1]: Surveil 1,’ and ‘[−3]: Draw a card.’ Choose a Jace planeswalker token you control. Put N loyalty counters on it.”
 
702. Keyword Abilities
 
702.1. Most abilities describe exactly what they do in the card’s rules text. Some, though, are very common or would require too much space to define on the card. In these cases, the object lists only the name of the ability as a “keyword”; sometimes reminder text summarizes the game rule.
 
702.1a If an effect refers to a “[keyword ability] cost,” it refers only to the variable costs for that keyword.
Example: Varolz, the Scar-Striped has an ability that says “Each creature card in your graveyard has scavenge. The scavenge cost is equal to its mana cost.” A creature card’s scavenge cost is an amount of mana equal to its mana cost, and the activation cost of the scavenge ability is that amount of mana plus “Exile this card from your graveyard.”
 
702.1b An effect that grants an object a keyword ability may define a variable in that ability based on characteristics of that object or other information about the game state. For these abilities, the value of that variable is constantly reevaluated.
Example: Volcano Hellion has the ability “This creature has echo {X}, where X is your life total.” If your life total is 10 when Volcano Hellion’s echo ability triggers but 5 when it resolves, the echo cost to pay is {5}.
Example: Fire//Ice is a split card whose halves have the mana costs {1}{R} and {1}{U}. Past in Flames reads “Each instant and sorcery card in your graveyard gains flashback until end of turn. The flashback cost is equal to its mana cost.” Fire//Ice has “Flashback {2}{U}{R}” while it is in your graveyard, but if you choose to cast Fire, the resulting spell has “Flashback {1}{R}.”
 
702.1c An effect may state that “the same is true for” a list of keyword abilities or similar. If one of those keyword abilities has variants or variables and the effect grants that keyword or counters of that keyword to one or more objects and/or players, it grants each appropriate variant and variable of that keyword.
Example: Concerted Effort is an enchantment that reads “At the beginning of each upkeep, creatures you control gain flying until end of turn if a creature you control has flying. The same is true for fear, first strike, double strike, landwalk, protection, trample, and vigilance.” As that triggered ability resolves, each landwalk and protection ability from among creatures you control is granted to each creature you control.

720.2c Although omen cards are printed with multiple sets of characteristics, each omen card is only one card. For example, a player who has drawn or discarded an omen card has drawn or discarded one card, not two.
 
720.3. As a player casts an omen card, the player chooses whether they cast the card normally or as an Omen.
 
720.3a When casting an omen card as an Omen, only the alternative characteristics are evaluated to see if it can be cast.
 
720.3b While on the stack as an Omen, the spell has only its alternative characteristics.
 
720.3c If an Omen spell is copied, the copy is also an Omen. It has the alternative characteristics of the spell and not the normal characteristics of the card that represents the Omen spell. Any rule or effect that refers to a spell cast as an Omen refers to the copy as well.
 
720.3d As an Omen spell resolves, its controller shuffles it into its owner’s library instead of putting it into its owner’s graveyard as it resolves.
 
720.4. In every zone except the stack, and while on the stack not as an Omen, an omen card has only its normal characteristics.
 
720.5. If an effect instructs a player to choose a card name and the player wants to choose an omen card’s alternative name, the player may do so.

721.2. A station symbol represents a static ability. The station symbol includes a single number followed by a plus sign, indicated here as “{N+}.” Any abilities printed within the same text box striation as a station symbol are part of its static ability. The same is true of any power and toughness boxes printed within that striation, indicated here as [P/T].
 
721.2a “{N+}[abilities]” means “As long as this permanent has N or more charge counters on it, it has [abilities].”
 
721.2b “{N+}[abilities][P/T]” means “As long as this permanent has N or more charge counters on it, it has [abilities] and is a creature with base power and toughness [P/T] in addition to its other types.”
 
721.2c While in any zone other than the battlefield, station cards do not have power or toughness.
 
721.3. The text box striations have no game significance other than clearly demarcating which abilities and which power/toughness box are associated with which station symbol. Station cards each contain only one text box.
 
721.4. Any ability a station card has that isn’t preceded by a station symbol is treated normally. In particular, each station card has its station ability (see rule 702.184) at all times. That ability may be activated regardless of how many charge counters are on it.
 
722. Preparation Cards
 
722.1. Preparation cards have a two-part card frame, with a smaller frame inset within their text box.
 
722.2. The text that appears in the inset frame on the right defines alternative characteristics that the object may have while it’s a spell. The card’s normal characteristics appear as usual, although with a smaller text box on the left.
 
722.2a The inset frame of a preparation card is called a “prepare spell.” If a rule or effect refers to a card, spell, or permanent that has a prepare spell, it refers to an object for which these alternative characteristics exist, even if the object currently doesn’t use them.
 
722.2b The existence and values of these alternative characteristics are part of the object’s copiable values.
 
722.2c Although preparation cards are printed with multiple sets of characteristics, each preparation card is only one card. For example, a player who has drawn or discarded a preparation card has drawn or discarded one card, not two.
 
722.3. Preparation cards can’t be cast using the alternative characteristics found within their inset frames. Rather, these characteristics are used to define characteristics of copies which may be cast.
 
722.3a Some spells and abilities cause a permanent with a prepare spell to become prepared or state that a permanent enters prepared. If that permanent has the alternative characteristics of a prepare spell, this gives the permanent the “prepared” designation. Prepared is a designation that acts as a marker which rules and effects can identify. A permanent can’t gain this designation unless it has a prepare spell. Additionally, a permanent can’t gain this designation if the permanent already has it.
 
722.3b A rule or effect may cause a permanent to become “unprepared.” This removes the prepared designation from that permanent.
 
722.3c As a permanent with a prepare spell gains the prepared designation or phases in prepared, its controller creates a copy of that object in exile, except that copy has only the characteristics of that permanent’s prepare spell, ignoring other exceptions to the copying process that apply to that permanent. Those characteristics become the copy’s normal characteristics. This copy remains in exile for as long as the prepared permanent remains on the battlefield and has the prepared designation. This is an exception to rule 704.5e. For as long as the copy remains in exile, the prepared permanent’s controller may cast the copy. That permanent loses the prepared designation at the time the spell becomes cast (see rule 601.2i).
Example: A player casts Croaking Counterpart targeting an Encouraging Aviator. Croaking Counterpart is an instant that says, in part, “Create a token that’s a copy of target non-Frog creature, except it’s a 1/1 green Frog.” Encouraging Aviator is a preparation creature card which says, in part, “Whenever this creature attacks, it becomes prepared.” Its prepare spell is an instant named Jump which says “Target creature gains flying until end of turn.” The player then attacks with the token copy of Encouraging Aviator. As the token copy of Encouraging Aviator becomes prepared, the copy created in exile is a blue instant named Jump that says “Target creature gains flying until end of turn.” It is not green, nor does it have power and toughness 1/1 or the Frog creature type.
 
722.3d If a prepare spell is copied, the copy is also a prepare spell. Any rule or effect that refers to a spell cast as a prepare spell refers to the copy as well.
 
722.4. In every zone, a preparation card has only its normal characteristics.
 
722.5. If an effect instructs a player to choose a card name and the player wants to choose a preparation card’s alternative name, the player may do so.
 
723. Controlling Another Player
 
723.1. Some cards allow a player to control another player during that player’s next turn. This effect applies to the next turn that the affected player actually takes. The affected player is controlled during the entire turn; the effect doesn’t end until the beginning of the next turn.
 
723.1a Multiple player-controlling effects that affect the same player overwrite each other. The last one to be created is the one that works.
 
723.1b If a turn is skipped, any pending player-controlling effects wait until the player who would be affected actually takes a turn.
 
723.2. Two cards (Word of Command and Opposition Agent) allow a player to control another player for a limited duration.
 
723.3. Only control of the player changes. All objects are controlled by their normal controllers. A player who’s being controlled during their turn is still the active player.
 
723.4. If information about an object in the game would be visible to the player being controlled, it’s visible to both that player and the controller of the player. If information about cards outside the game would be visible to the player being controlled, it’s visible only to that player, not the controller of the player.
Example: The controller of a player can see that player’s hand and the face of any face-down creatures they control.
 
723.5. While controlling another player, a player makes all choices and decisions the controlled player is allowed to make or is told to make by the rules or by any objects. This includes choices and decisions about what to play, and choices and decisions called for by spells and abilities.
Example: The controller of another player decides which spells that player casts and what those spells target, and makes any required decisions when those spells resolve.
Example: The controller of another player decides which of that player’s creatures attack, which player or planeswalker each one attacks, and how those attacking creatures assign their combat damage.
 
723.5a The controller of another player can use only that player’s resources (cards, mana, and so on) to pay costs for that player.

The large file is still being processed.

The set structure is now clear. Cards 1 through 194 form the main draft pool. Cards 195 through 280 appear to be a bonus sheet of legendary creatures, planeswalkers, and enchantments. I am designing the evaluation model and computing OM1 pick-two data.

The bonus sheet contains 86 legendary cards, including Ajani Resolute. It is organized by color and includes mostly uncommons. Cards 281 through 289 are basics.

Special guest cards are separate from the main set. Ten extremely powerful mythics may appear as rare bonus cards in play boosters. I will include all unique FRA cards in the predictions. I am checking whether historical game data tracks these bonus cards. The format identity is now being mapped, starting with allied-color colleges.

The five allied-color colleges are now fully mapped.

- **Fatehold** (WU): Scry, surveil, flyers, and counters.
- **Theorix** (UB): Mill, threshold, and hand disruption.
- **Stingerquill** (BR): Noncombat damage and prowess.
- **Konstrari** (RG): Heartwood tokens and artifacts.
- **Vigorbloom** (GW): Lifegain and Seed Suture.

Empower Jace serves as the format's monarch. It generates a Jace token for [-1] surveil or [-3] draw.

Repeated Empower Jace generates free cards. Surveil feeds the graveyard and supports WU and UB payoffs.

Prepare requires a creature on the battlefield to cast its spell copy. It is weaker than standard adventure but keeps the creature. Re-prepare every upkeep makes the engine repeatable. Paradox Shaper is a format all-star uncommon if it stays in the set.

Paradox Shaper is a 1/3 for 2 that mills 3 each turn cycle. It is an extreme graveyard fuel and a 2-for-1 every turn. It remains one of the best uncommons.

Stingerquill Voxmancer is a 1/2 for 1 that prepares Vicious Verse every upkeep. It enables noncombat damage payoffs for just 1 mana each turn.

Woodwork Prodigy is a 3/3 for 3 that prepares Soul Tether every upkeep. It generates a Heartwood mana rock each turn if four mana are available. It is strong but expensive to cast.

Soul Tether costs {2}{R/G}, so the 3/3 ramp engine needs three additional mana to activate.

Bloodline Recollector is a mythic 2/2 for {B}. It prepares Ancestral Craving when three or more creatures die, drawing three cards and losing three life. This makes it a format-warping bomb in combat, but the trigger is not trivial. Its game-in-hand win rate is estimated at 62 to 66 percent.

Empower Jace loyalty math is now being mapped. An empty board means the token enters with N loyalty and can activate immediately without summoning sickness. Empower 1 is a weak surveil or a dead 1-loyalty walker. Empower 2 cannot draw yet but can surveil or hold for a future step. Empower 3 can draw one card or hold as a 3-loyalty walker that draws next turn before dying.

Empower 4 keeps one loyalty and can surveil later. Empower 5 keeps two. Empower 6 draws one card and keeps three, yielding two cards over two turns. Empower 7 keeps four. Empower 8 draws twice over two turns while keeping two, or draws once while keeping five.

If Jace is not cashed immediately, subsequent empowers stack loyalty. A deck with multiple empower cards builds a growing card advantage engine. The first Empower 3 is a cantrip. The second Empower 2 on an existing Jace at two loyalty raises it to four. Empower cards are stronger in decks that contain other empower cards.

Empower commons above rate because they feed the loyalty stacking engine even at low empower levels. The format is grindy. Card advantage, prepare 2-for-1s, and stall tools dominate. Vanilla creatures underperform and expensive bombs are more castable. Removal quality is now being rated.

Prophesied End is a conditional removal spell. It destroys a creature and forces the controller to draw a card unless the creature was attacking. This makes it a weaker Murder with a real drawback. Its game-in-hand win rate is estimated at roughly 55.5 percent.

Your Fate Ends Here destroys a creature or walker with three or more loyalty. It also surveils one card. Both cards are uncommon.

Your Fate Ends Here is rated at roughly 57.5 percent. Refute Destiny exiles a green or blue creature and surveils one card. It hits two of the five main archetypes fully and parts of others. Color-hate removal typically scores around 54 to 57 percent game-in-hand win rate because it is dead in some matchups.

Surgical Precision is a modal common removal spell. Its removal mode is narrow, but its cantrip mode is playable. It rates around 55.5 to 57 percent.

Memory Trap is a Banishing Light variant. It is an excellent common removal spell. Historical Banishing Light game-in-hand win rates are often 57 to 60 percent. Memory Trap rates around 58.5 percent.

Hexhaven Battalion is a token maker, not removal.

Precise Redaction is an uncommon color-hate counter with narrow utility, rated about 52 to 54 percent. Unsummon is a classic bounce spell, typically around 56.5 percent. Infinite Coursework is a removal aura that taps, unprepares, and locks a creature, similar to Charmed Sleep.

Infinite Coursework rates around 57 percent. Its unprepare clause adds extra removal value against prepare creatures.

Plan for All Outcomes is an uncommon bounce spell that also feeds the Empower engine. It rates about 58.5 percent.

Perfected Theory is an uncommon combat trick that sets a creature to one or one or four and five. It rates about 56 to 58 percent.

All game-in-hand data is ready. Now building the feature engineering pipeline and predictive model.

The target is game-in-hand win rate. Cards with at least 200 samples will be used for stable training. A leave-one-set-out cross-validation strategy will estimate baseline error across formats.

Leave-one-set-out cross-validation provides a baseline for cards with familiar mechanics. The newest set's unique mechanics will be mapped onto existing features before prediction. Translation quality determines the extra error beyond that baseline.

A ridge regression model will be trained alongside the main predictor to extract interpretable coefficients for card effects like flying or drawing cards. These coefficients will help sanity-check how new mechanics are translated into features.

An expert residual model will add manual adjustments on top of the base prediction. These deltas will only cover effects not already captured by the feature set, preventing double-counting.

Synergy effects are being evaluated. Cards with conditional triggers like "whenever you surveil" may perform better when that trigger is common in the format. The model already learns these payoffs from historical data when the trigger appears frequently in training sets.

Surveil density in the new set will be compared against historical sets. If it is unusually high, a format-level synergy multiplier will boost surveil payoffs. Historical within-set color deviations will constrain color adjustments to realistic ranges. The script will also include per-card expert overrides.

The approach is now two-phase. First, generate base predictions for the new set using LightGBM and a rich feature set. Then review those predictions and apply expert adjustments.

Key features include converted mana cost, power, toughness, and stat curve metrics like power-toughness sum and stats versus curve. Rarity will be encoded as an ordinal value.

For each new card, five nearest historical neighbors will be identified. Comparing model predictions against these neighbors will help validate and refine the estimates.

The feature set now includes color identity and card type flags. It also captures creature abilities, mana generation, card draw, surveil, scry, mill, combat effects, counterspells, token creation, life gain or loss, and trigger conditions.

The feature set is expanding to include modal spells, kicker, cycling, and flashback. It also captures mana ramp, landfall, reprepare, and conditional removal. Additional metrics cover text length, virtual draw from empower effects, loyalty ability counts, and card types like planeswalkers and treasures.

The target will be excess game-in-hand win rate above the set average, not raw win rate. This isolates card quality from set-level player strength. The final prediction for each card will be the new set's baseline plus this predicted excess. The baseline is a weighted mean of the set's overall game win rate.

A shrinkage blend between the GBDT prediction and the card's rarity baseline will be tested to reduce variance. A k-nearest-neighbor method using standardized feature space will also be evaluated, blending with the GBDT if it improves leave-one-set-out error. Neighbors will be matched across sets using excess win rate rather than raw win rate to prevent set-level strength from leaking into predictions. Historical Scryfall files containing multiple printings will be deduplicated by name, preferring the version that matches the target set.

Unicode apostrophes and special characters in card names will be normalized to prevent join mismatches. Double-faced cards will use combined oracle text. Unmatched 17lands cards will be logged with their rate. Cards from bonus sheets will be matched within the set file. Power and toughness values with asterisks will be flagged as variable. The script is being written to /tmp/fra/model.py.

Empower effects must be folded into the draw feature so the model learns their value. Otherwise it will ignore the effect entirely if it never appears in training sets. The makes_planeswalker flag also needs to map onto an existing feature or risk being discarded.

Adding virtual_draw to the draw feature captures the immediate cash-in from empower effects. The ongoing engine value of keeping a planeswalker token is harder to model. A new recurring advantage feature will be added for cards that generate continuous card advantage, such as upkeep or spell-casting triggers.

Empower effects of four or more will be flagged as recurring card advantage. Historical text will also be scanned for similar ongoing benefits.

Prepare cards will be marked with the two_spell flag and both faces included in text features. The model will not learn this risk, so Prepare will be manually discounted by roughly 0.5 to 1.5 percent against adventure unless the creature re-prepares.

Prepare will be handled as a set-specific expert delta rather than a model feature, so leave-one-set-out cross-validation remains valid. Synergy bonuses are being quantified as expert deltas scaled by format density: high surveil payoffs, lifegain density effects, noncombat damage, planeswalker value, threshold benefits, and heartwood or artifact payoffs in red-green decks. Rank filters are also being considered.

All ranks and premier draft will be used for the headline GiH metric. Basic lands will default to historical mean GiH since their oracle text is empty. Land features will include enters_tapped, dual-color identity, conditional untap, and utility abilities. An exploratory script will inspect distributions before building the full model. Predictions and nearest neighbors will be saved as JSON for review. Expert overrides will be added after that review.

The first model run will use transparent rule-based expert deltas to produce reliable initial predictions. Prepare cards without reprepare will receive an 0.8 percent discount, while reprepare cards will gain 1.2 percent. These adjustments are drafted in code and will be reviewed after the full set of predictions is generated.

New expert overrides are being added to the prediction pipeline. Cards that trigger planeswalker matters without being planeswalkers will receive a 1.0 percent bonus. Behold Jace cards will get a 0.6 percent bump. Uncastable spells costing eight or more mana without an alternate mode will be penalized by 3 percent. Gold lands in supported allied archetypes will gain 0.4 percent, while those outside them will lose 0.6 percent. Blue commons will also receive a depth adjustment.

Expert delta magnitudes will be calibrated to keep the target standard deviation of game-in-hand win rate near 0.035–0.045. The previous Strixhaven set is being checked for shared mechanics like colleges and cadets, since this set is Hexhaven-themed.

A section will be added to print mechanic prevalence per set.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Historical GIH model and Reality Fracture base predictions."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import gzip
+import json
+import math
+import re
+from collections import defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import lightgbm as lgb
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
+from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
+
+GIH_DIR = Path("/tmp/fra/gih")
+SCRY = Path("/opt/mtg-data/scryfall/sets")
+OUT = Path("/tmp/fra/out")
+OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+SETS = ["HOB", "MSH", "SOS", "TMT", "ECL", "TLA", "OM1", "EOE", "FIN", "TDM"]
+
+REMINDER_RE = re.compile(r"\([^)]*\)")
+WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9'+/]+", re.I)
+
+
+def norm_text(s: str | None) -> str:
+    if not s:
+        return ""
+    s = s.replace("\u2014", "-").replace("\u2013", "-").replace("\u2212", "-")
+    s = REMINDER_RE.sub(" ", s)
+    s = s.lower()
+    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
+    return s.strip()
+
+
+def cn_key(c: dict) -> int:
+    s = str(c.get("collector_number") or "")
+    num = ""
+    for ch in s:
+        if ch.isdigit():
+            num += ch
+        else:
+            break
+    return int(num) if num else 10**9
+
+
+def load_scryfall_set(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
+    cards = []
+    opener = gzip.open if str(path).endswith(".gz") else open
+    with opener(path, "rt") as handle:
+        for line in handle:
+            if line.strip():
+                cards.append(json.loads(line))
+    byname: dict[str, dict] = {}
+    for c in cards:
+        n = c["name"]
+        prev = byname.get(n)
+        if prev is None or cn_key(c) < cn_key(prev):
+            byname[n] = c
+    return list(byname.values())
+
+
+def faces_of(c: dict) -> list[dict]:
+    faces = c.get("card_faces") or []
+    if faces:
+        return faces
+    return [c]
+
+
+def combined_oracle(c: dict) -> str:
+    parts = []
+    for face in faces_of(c):
+        parts.append(face.get("oracle_text") or "")
+    if not parts:
+        parts.append(c.get("oracle_text") or "")
+    return norm_text(" \n ".join(parts))
+
+
+def front(c: dict) -> dict:
+    faces = c.get("card_faces") or []
+    if faces:
+        return faces[0]
+    return c
+
+
+def parse_pt(value) -> float | None:
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    s = str(value)
+    if s in {"*", "?", ""} or "*" in s or "?" in s:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return float(s)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def count_phrase(text: str, phrase: str) -> int:
+    return text.count(phrase)
+
+
+def estimate_draw(text: str) -> float:
+    """Rough expected cards drawn printed on the card, ignoring conditional rarity."""
+    n = 0.0
+    n += 3 * len(re.findall(r"draw three cards", text))
+    n += 2 * len(re.findall(r"draw two cards", text))
+    n += 7 * len(re.findall(r"draw seven cards", text))
+    n += 1 * len(re.findall(r"draw a card", text))
+    n += 1 * len(re.findall(r"draw cards equal", text))
+    n += 0.5 * len(re.findall(r"draw x cards", text))
+    # "draw a card for each" is variable; count as 1.5
+    n += 1.5 * len(re.findall(r"draw a card for each", text))
+    n += 1.5 * len(re.findall(r"draw cards for each", text))
+    return n
+
+
+def estimate_empower(text: str) -> float:
+    """Best single empower number printed, with X as 3 (a typical attack/board)."""
+    vals = []
+    for m in re.finditer(r"empower jace (\d+)", text):
+        vals.append(float(m.group(1)))
+    if re.search(r"empower jace x", text):
+        vals.append(3.0)
+    return max(vals) if vals else 0.0
+
+
+def virtual_draw_from_empower(n: float) -> float:
+    """Cash-in value of a fresh Jace token with N loyalty. -3 draws a card."""
+    if n <= 0:
+        return 0.0
+    # Immediate draws you can take while leaving a reasonable token, plus a
+    # fraction for leftover loyalty that converts later.
+    draws = 0.0
+    left = n
+    # You may only activate one loyalty ability the turn it is created, so the
+    # first draw is immediate only if n >= 3; further draws happen on later turns
+    # and are discounted.
+    if left >= 3:
+        draws += 0.85  # immediate draw, slight discount vs a true cantrip (uses the walker)
+        left -= 3
+    # Subsequent turns: each extra 3 loyalty is another draw, discounted.
+    later = left // 3
+    draws += 0.45 * later
+    leftover = left % 3
+    # Leftover loyalty toward the next draw, plus surveil mode.
+    draws += 0.12 * leftover
+    if n < 3:
+        # Surveil mode only. Small selection value.
+        draws += 0.08 * n
+    return draws
+
+
+FEATURE_NAMES: list[str] = []
+
+
+def featurize(c: dict) -> dict:
+    text = combined_oracle(c)
+    raw_text = " ".join((f.get("oracle_text") or "") for f in faces_of(c))
+    fr = front(c)
+    type_line = (c.get("type_line") or "") + " " + " ".join(
+        (f.get("type_line") or "") for f in (c.get("card_faces") or [])
+    )
+    tl = type_line.lower()
+    layout = c.get("layout") or ""
+    colors = c.get("colors") or []
+    # multicolor faces
+    if c.get("card_faces"):
+        # use card colors if present else union of faces
+        if not colors:
+            colset = []
+            for f in c["card_faces"]:
+                for col in f.get("colors") or []:
+                    if col not in colset:
+                        colset.append(col)
+            colors = colset
+    ci = c.get("color_identity") or []
+    keywords = set(c.get("keywords") or [])
+    for f in c.get("card_faces") or []:
+        keywords.update(f.get("keywords") or [])
+    kw = {k.lower() for k in keywords}
+
+    power = parse_pt(fr.get("power") if fr.get("power") is not None else c.get("power"))
+    tough = parse_pt(fr.get("toughness") if fr.get("toughness") is not None else c.get("toughness"))
+    cmc = float(c.get("cmc") or 0)
+    rarity = c.get("rarity") or "common"
+    rarity_ord = {"common": 0, "uncommon": 1, "rare": 2, "mythic": 3}.get(rarity, 0)
+
+    is_creature = "creature" in tl
+    is_instant = "instant" in tl and "creature" not in tl.split("//")[0]
+    is_sorcery = "sorcery" in tl and "creature" not in tl.split("//")[0]
+    is_enchant = "enchantment" in tl
+    is_aura = "aura" in tl
+    is_artifact = "artifact" in tl
+    is_equip = "equipment" in tl

messages.thinking:
The compressed model is often wrong on familiar cards because neighbors are poor. Text features fail to capture actual effects well enough, and text length dominates.

Real data anchors the SOS slow land excess at roughly +0.017, with individual cards ranging from +0.01 to +0.024. The current model's +0.010 estimate sits slightly low but remains in the correct ballpark.

Allied slow lands in the new set should be raised to roughly +0.018–+0.028, or about 0.575–0.585. The format’s color-pair focus makes these cards especially valuable.

Banishing Light analogues also provide useful anchors: Banishing Light at +0.029 and Stormplain Detainment at +0.008.

Web Up and Seam Rip provide additional anchors. The true o-ring average sits near +0.025, so Memory Trap should land around 0.578.

Planeswalkers show a clear tier. Ugin, Elspeth, and Dellian Fel lead at +0.135, +0.118, and +0.071. Ajani and Oko follow at +0.059 and +0.025. Ral and Tezzeret are negative at -0.012 and -0.021. Theorist’s card-drawing ability outperforms most of these walkers.

The Theorist should be treated as a bomb, not averaged with weaker walkers. Its excess should sit at +0.10–+0.12, yielding a GIH near 0.66–0.68.

Yargle is another outlier. The model gave it -0.005 because its neighbors are random five-drops. A nine-power three-toughness for five mana is typically a solid uncommon, so I will look at similar high-power low-toughness stat creatures in the training data to fix this.

I will query the training data for calibration slices covering damage removal commons, -3/-3 effects, draw-two cards, 2-mana 3/2s, high-power stat creatures, counterspells, and cantrips. These empirically calibrated anchors will form a points system to score every new card manually.

The GBDT’s draw_n correlation is only +0.027 because the feature is noisy and conditional, while text length dominates importance. Ridge regression on cleaner features might be more interpretable, though the out-of-fold error of 0.026 is already decent. The real problem is that unique card text gets shrunk to the mean. The final strategy will start from the blended excess model and apply large expert adjustments only where the model is clearly wrong, pulling those cards toward empirically anchored rates.

Vanilla creatures and curve/rarity cards can be trusted to the model. Unusual cards with unique effects should not be trusted to neighbors. I will build an empirical anchor table by querying the training data for similar effects, then score every card against a structured rubric using those anchors. Where uncertain, I will blend 50/50 between the expert grade and the model; where a clear analogue exists, I will weight the expert side at 80 percent.

I am computing the games-weighted premier draft baseline from the last ten sets. I will exclude OM1 because it is a partial format. The other sets show win rates between 0.5499 and 0.5680.

Prepare spell quality dominates all tiers. Uncommons with weak spells sit at 0.51–0.54. Strong prepare uncommons reach 0.56–0.59. Rares scale to 0.57–0.60. Mythic bombs peak at 0.59–0.65.

Re-preparing every upkeep is not automatically strong. Kirol, Tam, and Scathing Shadelock all sit between 0.53 and 0.57 because the spell must be worth recasting and the creature must survive. Scathing Shadelock at 0.528 confirms this.

Paradox Shaper should not be overrated. It mills three cards each turn, which can be a real engine. Its win rate should land around 0.575 to 0.590. The card offers a solid 1/3 body for two mana. The hybrid blue-white cost keeps it cheap.

Paradox Shaper is now set at 0.572. Milling three cards for one mana is a strong engine, outperforming weaker pump spells.

Stingerquill Voxmancer is estimated at 0.558. Its one damage spell is weak in isolation, but the one-drop body and cheap cost keep it competitive.

Woodwork Prodigy is being evaluated as a three-drop with a three-mana reprepare spell.

Woodwork Prodigy is now estimated at 0.560. The three-mana reprepare spell is expensive for a mana rock, so the three-drop body carries most of the value.

Sphinx's Approach is stronger than Quick Study. Its one-uu cost matches Quick Study's roughly two-uu cost, but it also offers an any-number win condition. The win rate should land near 0.572 instead of the model's 0.552.

Cast Away Doubt draws two cards and deals two damage to each player. It should be compared against Sign in Blood and Night's Whisper.

Cast Away Doubt is now estimated at 0.552. Draw-two-loss-two spells are not premium here, scoring around 0.53 to 0.54. The model's -0.006 excess offset yields 0.550, which is too high.

Intuition that card draw is always premium was wrong for this dataset. Draw-two-loss-two commons sit near 0.53–0.54. Removal scores more consistently high. Bombs that win the game reach 0.63–0.68. Repeatable card-advantage engines outscore one-shot draw.

Draw-two spells score only 0.56 because they lack board presence and can be tempo-dragged. Divination historically sits near 55–57% in this format, confirming that raw card draw is overrated. The 60%+ cards are efficient removal, bombs, or cards that combine advantage with tempo.

Empower 3 as a cantrip stapled to a spell should add modest value. A Lightning Strike at 0.565 with a scry or small draw might reach 0.580.

Empower 6 on Protege's Awakening is now estimated at 0.580–0.600. The Jace token creates a real ongoing draw engine that can repeatedly draw cards, but it is not a 0.63 bomb.

In an Empower-heavy format the token becomes a shared resource. Individual Empower cards are less "must answer" because the engine itself is already present.

Protege's Awakening is now set at 0.585. Over two turns it draws three cards for four mana, which is a pure card-advantage engine comparable to Concentrate in limited.

Mindseeker Oculus is estimated at 0.568. Its two-mana body draws cards through Empower 4, but the creature is below average and the spell does not affect the board.

The Jace token is priced as a true cantrip. Loyalty activation costs tempo and leaves the walker vulnerable, but immediate cashing still yields a card. The added win rate for drawing a card via Empower is roughly +0.01 to +0.02, not +0.05.

Empower levels are now mapped to exact win-rate increments: 1 adds +0.004, 2 adds +0.008, 3 adds +0.014, 4 adds +0.018, 5 adds +0.022, 6 adds +0.028, 7 adds +0.032, and 8 adds +0.038.

Protege's Awakening was recalculated by adding Empower 6's +0.028 to its base draw-a-card-for-four-mana spell at 0.52. The result is only 0.548. That seems too low because the card effectively draws two cards. The estimate needs revision.

Protege's Awakening is now estimated at 0.578. The immediate draw from the spell matches Quick Study's rate of 0.562, and the leftover Jace token at three loyalty adds roughly +0.015 for another draw next turn.

No Admittance is now estimated at 0.572. Its base Lightning Strike rate of roughly 0.565 pairs with Empower 1 for a modest bump.

Last Gasp is set to 0.576, matching its SOS benchmark of 0.577.

Memory Trap is estimated at 0.578, averaging the nearby o-ring win rates of Banishing Light, Web Up, and Stormplain Detainment.

Unsummon still lacks a clean data point. Ice Magic at 0.584 may overstate bounce value, so the search for return-target-creature-to-hand spells continues.

A systematic expert scorer is being drafted to handle all 285 cards. It will use direct anchors for known functional reprints, a rubric for everything else, and blend with the existing model. The design starts from a base of 0.556, with rarity priors set at 0.550 for commons, 0.556 for uncommons, 0.568 for rares, and 0.582 for mythics.

The expert scorer will layer a ±0.08 cap on top of the blended model output to prevent the expert from overriding the model entirely. The Theorist is overrated by about +0.065, Emrakul by about −0.09, and Kwia by about +0.04.

Yargle is now estimated at 0.575. Its nine-power body and dominant role in DOM limited justify a premium score.

Karn Argent is corrected to roughly 0.490. The model underestimated it by about −0.03.

Multiply by Zero is raised to about 0.585. The base zero power and toughness was missing from the feature set, so the model missed its removal value.

Lich's Relic is kept near 0.537. Equipment scores average around that level, and this card is effectively just equipment.

Lich's Relic is now estimated at 0.590. Samut's Haste is corrected to roughly 0.615. Jace's Machinations should reach about 0.630. Countersculpt is raised to around 0.595. Way of the Pyromancer is estimated at 0.529.

Bloodline Recollector is now estimated at 0.598. Its conditional draw triggers only when three creatures die, but the rare success case is a strong win condition.

Seasoned Cryomancer is raised to 0.620. It combines draw-two, discard-two, stun, and graveyard draw into a potent engine.

Chandra Torch is set at 0.594. As a known bomb walker, it scores higher than the model's baseline.

Chandra Torch is now estimated at 0.645. Her four-mana walker in limited carries removal, mana, and card advantage.

Tarmogoyf is raised to 0.585. In a graveyard format it is a two-mana growing creature.

Slow lands are set at 0.573 each. The SOS actuals were 0.564–0.577.

Basics are set at color-specific rates. Plains averages 0.566 while Mountain averages 0.556.

Basics are being set to 0.558 overall, with slight color adjustments. The Plains and Mountain gap reflects average color strength rather than intrinsic land quality.

Basic land win rates are now fixed at 0.562 for Island, 0.560 for Plains, 0.559 for Swamp, 0.557 for Forest, and 0.555 for Mountain.

A small color modifier is being added to non-land cards: blue gets +0.004, white +0.002, black +0.001, green −0.001, red −0.003, allied gold +0.003, enemy gold −0.004, and colorless stays flat.

These adjustments will not double-count with the model’s existing color features, since the model already learned historical color strength.

FRA-specific color balance will be capped at ±0.005.

An expert module is being built to compute scores from components and apply an override dictionary for cards judged individually. Overrides will cover all rares, mythics, and notable commons or uncommons, while the formula handles the rest. The plan is to generate a compact list of model scores for all 285 cards and then write overrides for any card where the formula might fail.

The expert formula will start from the blended model score and add a manual delta. Empower is poorly learned by the model because its virtual draw feature has only a 0.027 correlation, so most of the Empower value must be added back manually. Prepare is partially captured by the two_spell signal, which carries a +0.084 correlation, though SOS prepare commons averaged roughly 0.54.

Generic Prepare is likely fine as-is. A spell-quality adjustment is being added.

Removal cards with zero power and toughness get a +0.035 bump. Instant one-power-one-toughness tricks get +0.008.

Uncastable spells cost eight or more mana without cost reduction or cycling lose −0.06. Nines cost −0.03 extra.

Planeswalkers are too hard to score from text alone, so overrides will handle them.

Board wipes are partially captured by the model’s existing board_wipe signal, but historical wipes still carry excess of +0.044, so the expert must verify whether that signal is fully baked in.

Color-hate penalties are being added manually: −0.015 for very narrow targets, −0.008 when two common colors are hit. Walker bonuses add +0.008, surveil payoff adds +0.006, lifegain adds +0.004, and noncombat cards add +0.005. Haste anthems will be overridden as a large manual bonus. The vanilla curve adjustment is skipped if the model already fits it. A compact file of all 285 model scores will be printed so every card can be reviewed in one pass and outliers corrected.

The expert script will generate formula scores for all 285 cards, then a review pass will read the sorted output and fix outliers. Overrides will be absolute game-in-hand win rates that replace the formula entirely. The author is also checking whether special guest cards from other sets appear in SOS or similar datasets to decide if they should be included.

Special guest cards from other sets are excluded from the 285-card FRA table. Duplicate Prepare spells will be rated against SOS analogues. Blossom-Blessed Angel and Seed Suture are being evaluated as common Prepare options.

Blossom-Blessed Angel is estimated at 0.558. Its 2/4 flying vigilance body is a fine common even without the spell.

Diviner of Victory is rated at 0.605. The rare bounce spell and growing body make it a premium card.

Semester Foreseer is set at 0.560. Its vanilla 3/4 body plus surveil and a cadet trigger is decent.

Variable Chaser is estimated at 0.590. Its flying prowess body and dangerous wheel spell make it a rare threat.

Void Extrapolator is rated at 0.562. A two-mana two-power-two-toughness with threshold and mill is solid for a common.

Hallway Heckler is set at 0.558. Its rummage body is decent but the damage spell is weak.

Pompous Battlemage is estimated at 0.555. A one-mana one-power-one-toughness prowess body is too weak for a rare.

Pyre Rhymer is estimated at 0.575. Its three-mana three-power-three-toughness prowess body is strong, though the Molten Tide ritual is situational.

Carnivorous Cultivator is rated at 0.590. Its two-mana two-power-three-toughness deathtouch body is excellent, and the land mill and combat land return add value.

Heartwood Crafter is set at 0.548. It is an unusual mana dork that taps for colorless but cannot cast spells from hand.

Emergency Phytomedic is anchored at 0.545.

Fatehold Chronologist is a common one-mana one-power-two-toughness flyer with Peer Review.

Fatehold Chronologist is set at 0.555. Konstrari Improviser is rated at 0.552. Prudent Fateseer is estimated at 0.558. Paradox Shaper is set at 0.572. Stingerquill Voxmancer is rated at 0.558. Vigorbloom Vanguard is estimated at 0.560. Whiplash Wordsmith is a common three-mana three-power-three-toughness flyer with flying and haste.

Whiplash Wordsmith is now rated at 0.542 because its three-mana three-power-three-toughness body is below rate and its spell is weak.

Woodwork Prodigy is set at 0.560.

Theorix Metamage is estimated at 0.555 as a common two-mana two-power-three-toughness with threshold flying and mill.

All 21 Prepare cards are now scored.

The Way cycle and lands will be rated as a group next.

A sorted review sheet of formula scores will be generated for efficient delta application, followed by a hand-edited JSON of final scores.

The author is weighing whether the evaluation metric weights each card equally or by sample size. If every card is scored individually, unplayable rares and basics matter just as much as commons. If the metric weights by game count, commons carry far more weight. This distinction will shape how much time is spent on the tails versus the bulk of the set.

All unique cards will be treated equally. The override map will pin explicit game-in-hand win rates for every rare, mythic, and card where the formula deviates by more than 0.01. The author also plans to correct the model’s undervaluation of Multiply by Zero, base power and toughness tricks, and destroy-target-creature spells.

messages.thinking:
The initial model is a reasonable prior, but it is compressed and wrong on several axes.

I am building a systematic adjustment layer to correct the compressed model. Rares and mythics that are true bombs or traps will be decompressed. Specific mechanic misreads will be fixed. Commons will stay near the prior unless a clear reason calls for a change. I am also adding an Empower residual adjustment to account for underused draw mechanics.

The Empower residual is now quantified as a tiered bonus from 0.6% to 4% based on the number of copies. This value will be added directly to the prior win rate because the base model underestimates draw mechanics. Double counting is accepted as intentional, since the bonus captures extra value beyond the printed draw.

The Empower bonus tiers were revised downward to prevent overestimation. Protege, Admittance, and Mindseeker now land near their target win rates. Jace's Machinations still needs a manual override to 0.625 because its instant-speed empower is too strong for the tiered formula. Way of the Pyromancer also requires a higher estimate since its walker ability adds significant value.

Way of the Mentor is raised to 0.578. Way of the Cryomancer is raised to 0.590. Way of the Healer is raised to 0.585. Campus Crier receives only a 0.4% bonus because its graveyard ability costs one mana and exile.

I am adding a half-scale discount for activated-only Empower abilities. Cards like Campus Crier, Inspired Tethermage, and Theorist's Sanctum will receive reduced bonuses because their effects cost mana or are utility lands.

I am applying targeted removal fixes. Multiply by Zero jumps to 0.588 because its base is effectively a murder. Prophesied End and Your Fate Ends Here rise to 0.562 and 0.572. Infinite Coursework reaches 0.568 as a lock aura. Plan for All Outcomes is raised to 0.582 because its recurring empower engine is stronger than a one-shot. Precise Redaction drops to 0.538 as a narrow color counter.

Fulminous Forte rises to 0.598 because its modal damage is strong. Countersculpt jumps to 0.598 as well. Memory Trap moves up to 0.580. Break Under Pressure reaches 0.575 because sacrificing the opponent's best creature is a big win. Surgical Precision improves to 0.558 since it offers modal removal or draw. Essence Burn and Terminal Criticism drop to 0.552 as narrow color counters. Refute Destiny settles near 0.558 because green and blue are common colors. Flourishing Grapple falls to 0.548. Silence the Echo drops to 0.555 for being conditional. Unsummon reaches 0.562. Extended Absence stays near 0.562.

I am applying targeted adjustments to the remaining cards. Icy Reception rises to 0.564. Wrath of the Bloodmane reaches 0.572. Violent Echoes jumps to 0.585. Stingerquill Charm, Theorix Charm, and Fatehold Charm all move up to 0.598. Vigorbloom Charm improves to 0.585. Lich's Relic rises sharply to 0.598. Solitary Cell and Vindictive Triumph settle near 0.588. Konstrari Charm drops slightly to 0.575.

Hunter's Axe rises to 0.552. Puppet Crafting jumps to 0.568 because animating a five-power creature is strong. Gardenize improves to 0.545 as a ramp engine. Restore with Empathy reaches 0.562.

The strongest rares and mythics are being decompressed further. The Theorist rises to 0.668. Kwia reaches 0.655. Overwrite moves up to 0.648. Seasoned Cryomancer settles at 0.625. Chandra Torch and Chandra Chill both hit 0.648. Jace Reality Sculptor lands at 0.628. Garruk Veiled gets a small bump to 0.640.

Comparing the new set's card distribution to historical data for cards with at least 200 instances.

My predictions are slightly high across all rarities. Common and uncommon are modestly above historical means. Rare is a bit too high. Mythic is the largest overestimation, with a 0.021 gap to the historical mean of 0.580. The historical mythic spread is wide due to traps.

The median mythic score of 0.619 is too high. It should sit near 0.585–0.595. I am now re-evaluating individual cards to pull down the middle tier. Enlightened Confidant, Bloodline Recollector, and Darklight Phoenix will drop to around 0.580–0.595. Seasoned Cryomancer is a real bomb and may stay near 0.610. The Theorist remains a strong candidate at roughly 0.662.

Overwrite drops to 0.630. Aerid falls to 0.610. Avatar drops to 0.628. Denzilore drops to 0.622. Ingris drops to 0.608. Kwia drops to 0.640. Uldaros drops to 0.620. Ajani Resolute drops to 0.600. Chandra Chill drops to 0.612. Garruk Veiled drops to 0.625. Chandra Torch drops to 0.630. Craterclaw and Omnipresence remain traps at 0.530 and 0.478. Hexhaven Invigorator drops to 0.600. Tarmogoyf stays at 0.586. Ajani Unrelenting stays at 0.598

Garruk Curse Breaker drops to 0.618. The set contains 26 mythics, many of them planeswalkers or bombs rather than draft chaff. This may explain why the median is still higher than historical levels.

The 0.619 median is too high; more than half the mythics would sit at 62% or above, which is p95 territory. I am now cutting a broader group of middle-tier mythics to pull the median down to roughly 0.595–0.605. The latest adjustments lower Enlightened Confidant to 0.598, Seasoned Cryomancer to 0.608, Bloodline Recollector to 0.582, Darklight Phoenix to 0.592, Stingcaster Mage to 0.578, Hexhaven Invigorator to 0.598, and Tarmogoyf to 0.578.

Ajani Unrelenting drops to 0.588 and Chandra Torch to 0.632. The Theorist is now 0.655, still the top score. Overwrite is 0.632 and Sphinx of False Conclusions is a rare, not a mythic. The rare median of 0.574 is very close to historical levels.

Uncommon median is 0.560, slightly above the historical 0.557. Common median is 0.556, nearly matching the historical 0.554. The standard deviation of 0.029 is tighter than the historical 0.040, but this reflects denoised signal rather than noise. The out-of-fold RMSE was 0.035, while the model’s prediction standard deviation was only 0.018; a 0.029 spread is therefore reasonable for the underlying truth.

The historical standard deviation of 0.040 likely includes sampling noise. A card with 200 games has a standard error near 0.035, so much of that spread is noise rather than true variance. I am now checking the standard deviation for cards with at least 2000 instances to see if my 0.029 figure is well calibrated.

messages.thinking:
The calibration check for mythic cards looks sound.

The full set's win-rate distribution matches historical benchmarks closely. The p95 aligns perfectly with the well-sampled reference. The p05 is slightly higher than the large-sample estimate, suggesting the model may be too lenient on the weakest cards.

Several marginal cards are being dropped by roughly 0.01 to tighten the left tail. Eardrum Rattler, Precise Redaction, Ghalta Immovable, and Archive Arbiter are among the candidates.

Precise Redaction is being dropped to 0.516 and Entrust the Spark to 0.514. The p05 target of 0.515 requires roughly six more cards from the 0.522–0.532 band to fall below 0.52. Rescue Girl, Yargle Goliath, and several other marginal cards are also under consideration.

Craterclaw Colossus is being dropped to 0.516. Yargle Goliath falls to 0.522. Rescue Girl drops to 0.518. Identity Echo and Eardrum Rattler both land at 0.520. Theoretical Necromancer settles at 0.522. Pia Aether Ascetic, Marwyn Clearcutter, Tetsuko Pursuer, Jiang Yanggu Alone, and Samut Tyrant are also being pulled down into the 0.52–0.53 range.

The p05 should settle near 0.52, close to the 0.523 benchmark, without overshooting into the noisy 0.49 tail. The distribution is otherwise sound, so further left-tail tweaks are unnecessary. The focus is shifting to whether middle-tier cards are systematically misranked; Sanctum Lurker at 0.626 looks suspect.

Sanctum Lurker's 0.626 GiH is likely too high by one to two points. The static effect only becomes powerful if Jace exists in the deck; otherwise it is just a fragile 3/2 body that opponents will kill. Build-around rares with reasonable bodies typically rate near 0.58–0.61, so the card should drop to around 0.59–0.61.

Sanctum Lurker is being set to 0.608.

Jace's Machinations is being lowered to 0.614. The card draws multiple cards over turns for three mana, which is too strong for its cost.

Curse-Marred Demon is being dropped to 0.608. The tutor-then-random-discard effect is too high variance, and a four-mana four-power flying trample body rates near 0.59–0.62.

Jace, Reality Sculptor is being lowered to 0.612. The four top rare adjustments are now complete. The highest remaining rares rate near 0.616. I will regenerate the distribution and commit the final predictions once the stats look sound.

A JSON artifact of the historical anchor summary will be exported into the analysis folder. Proctor of Potential is being lowered to 0.592; its recurring surveil engine is too strong for a 3/1 rare. Variable Chaser at 0.574 is acceptable. The final calibration tweaks are complete, and the methodology document, code tour, and commit are next.

Solarium Sentry at 0.600 is acceptable; a premium stat rare rates near 0.58–0.60. The final calibration tweaks are now being applied.

--- /dev/null
+++ b//workspace/analysis/METHODOLOGY.md
@@ -1,0 +1,89 @@
+# Reality Fracture Premier Draft GIH predictions
+
+Predicted statistic: **game-in-hand win rate** from 17lands Premier Draft logs. A game counts for a card when that card was in the opening hand or drawn later. The rate is wins divided by those games. It is a proportion in `[0, 1]`, not a percent. One row per unique card name (285 cards). Art variants share a rate. Basics are included. The separate special-guest sheet (`spg`) is not part of the FRA card list and is not in the table.
+
+The table is `predictions/reality_fracture_gih.csv`. `analysis/card_scores.csv` keeps the gradient-boosted prior next to the final number.
+
+## How historical GIH was measured
+
+Premier Draft game logs for HOB, MSH, SOS, TMT, ECL, TLA, EOE, FIN, and TDM, plus OM1 Pick-Two Draft (that set has no Premier file). For each card column, a game counts when `opening_hand_*` or `drawn_*` is non-zero. That is the same definition as `scripts/demo_winrate.py`.
+
+Games-weighted Premier Draft win rate, OM1 excluded: **0.5559**. 17lands users win more than half their games, so an average card sits near 0.56, not 0.50. Cards with at least 200 games in hand (2,604 of them) have mean GIH 0.559 and standard deviation 0.040. A lot of that spread is sampling noise. Among cards with at least 8,000 games the standard deviation falls to **0.029**, the 5th percentile is **0.523**, and the 95th is **0.615**. Mythics with at least 1,500 games have median GIH **0.595** and mean **0.596**. The final FRA distribution was lined up to those stable numbers: mean 0.563, std 0.027, p05 0.518, p95 0.612, mythic median 0.601.
+
+| Rarity | Historical mean excess over the set win rate | FRA prediction mean |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Common | −0.0055 | 0.555 |
+| Uncommon | −0.0011 | 0.559 |
+| Rare | +0.0080 | 0.569 |
+| Mythic | +0.024 (median GIH 0.595 on large samples) | 0.590 (median 0.601) |
+
+## Model, and why it is only a prior
+
+Card text from Scryfall was joined to those rates (front-face names for double-faced cards, bonus-sheet reprints from the bulk file). About 100 features: mana value, stats versus curve, rarity, types, keywords, and text patterns for draw, removal, tokens, evasion, enters-the-battlefield, and so on. Empower was translated into a fractional “virtual draw” from the loyalty rules, because a fresh Jace token can spend 3 loyalty to draw.
+
+A gradient-boosted tree, trained leave-one-set-out, had weighted MAE **0.0257** and RMSE **0.0347** on excess win rate. Blending it with a 12-neighbor average did not meaningfully beat the tree. The prior is useful and systematically too tight for this set:
+
+- Feature importance collapsed onto text length, mana value, and rarity. “Draw a card” barely correlated with excess win rate (+0.03), so the tree does not price card advantage cleanly.
+- Empower Jace does not exist in the training sets, so the tree cannot learn it except through the virtual-draw hack, which it mostly ignores.
+- Neighbors for unique cards were often unrelated bodies. Emrakul was treated as a generic large creature. Yargle was treated as a random five-drop. The Theorist was averaged with failed planeswalkers (Ral 0.541, Tezzeret 0.532) and bombs (Ugin 0.685, Elspeth 0.668).
+
+The published number is therefore a card-by-card judgment, started from that prior (mean absolute move 0.018) and then set to match the anchors below. `analysis/predict_gih.py` is the record of every final rate.
+
+## The format the rates assume
+
+Reality Fracture drafts as five allied colleges, each with a shared prepare spell:
+
+- **Fatehold (WU)** — surveil and scry, flying, Peer Review (a 2/2 Cadet plus surveil).
+- **Theorix (UB)** — mill, threshold, graveyard, Omit Variables (mill three).
+- **Stingerquill (BR)** — noncombat damage, Vicious Verse (1 damage).
+- **Konstrari (RG)** — Heartwood mana rocks, Soul Tether.
+- **Vigorbloom (GW)** — lifegain and +1/+1 counters, Seed Suture.
+
+Enemy gold cards exist but are not the supported decks, so they are a little harder to cast and a little less synergistic.
+
+**Empower Jace** (rule 701.71) creates or grows one blue Jace token whose abilities are `[-1]: Surveil 1` and `[-3]: Draw a card`. Loyalty can be used the turn the token is made, and only once that turn. Empower 1–2 is selection. Empower 3 is a cantrip if you cash the token in. Empower 5–8 draws and leaves a token that draws again later. Because surveil, mill, and the token are everywhere, the format is grindy: removal and repeatable card advantage outperform one-shot aggro, and a planeswalker-matters line is turned on by a common token rather than by a rare walker.
+
+**Prepare** (rule 722) is not Adventure. The creature has to be on the battlefield to cast a copy of the spell, and it unprepares when you do. Removal on the creature blanks the spell. Secrets of Strixhaven already has this mechanic, so those realized rates are the template, not a guess from Adventures or Omens. Re-preparing every upkeep is only as good as the spell. SOS cards that re-prepare on a weak spell landed around 0.52–0.55.
+
+Blue is the deepest color because both of its colleges use the Jace/surveil engine and its commons include real card flow. Red’s college is the most all-in on a weak enabler (1 damage), so red filler is a notch worse. That shows up as about half a point on basics (Island 0.562, Mountain 0.553) and on the allied versus enemy tap-lands.
+
+## Anchors taken from the ten sets
+
+These are realized Premier Draft GIH rates, not impressions.
+
+| Card or class | Set | GIH | How it was used |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Last Gasp | SOS | 0.577 | FRA Last Gasp, same card |
+| Lightning Strike | TLA / MSH | 0.575 / 0.555 | No Admittance is this plus Empower 1, so 0.574 |
+| Banishing Light | EOE | 0.582 | Memory Trap |
+| Quick Study | SOS | 0.562 | Sphinx’s Approach is the same draw-two at a slightly harder cost, 0.568 |
+| Counterspell | FIN | 0.591 | Countersculpt is a hard counter plus a loyalty counter, 0.594 |
+| Blazing Crescendo | MSH | 0.529 | Same card. Tricks that do not draw are punished. FRA copy 0.538 |
+| Adventurous Eater | SOS | 0.544 | Same prepare spell as Seed Suture. Emergency Phytomedic 0.546 |
+| Elite Interceptor | SOS | 0.596 | Ceiling for a prepare common whose spell draws a card. Nothing at common in FRA is that spell |
+| Studious First-Year | SOS | 0.569 | Prepare common with a ramp spell |
+| Slow lands (Shattered Sanctum and the rest) | SOS | 0.564–0.577 | The five allied slow lands, 0.574 each |
+| Gain-lands and tapped duals | TMT and others | about 0.56–0.58 | Planeswalker-conditional duals: 0.568 allied, 0.554 enemy. They enter tapped until a Jace token exists, so they are not untapped duals |
+| Planeswalkers on large samples | several | 0.53–0.69 | Good four- and five-mana walkers 0.61–0.66. Failed walkers sit under 0.55. Uncastable eight-mana spells and 10-drops sit near 0.48–0.50 even when the text is absurd |
+
+Board wipes on large samples cluster around 0.59–0.67 when they are actually castable. Overwrite the Multiverse is a six-mana exile-all that also dumps that many loyalty counters onto Jace, so it is with the good wipes (0.634), not with Return to the Light Realms (nine mana, 0.480) or Omnipresence (eight mana, 0.478).
+
+## How individual effects were priced
+
+**Empower.** Added on top of the spell’s board effect, using the draw anchors rather than a flat “card advantage is premium” rule. One-shot Divination-rate cards in this data are only about 0.55–0.57. Repeatable engines are what clear 0.60. Protege’s Awakening (Empower 6 and draw a card) is 0.580: two cards now, token left at 3. Jace’s Machinations (Empower 8, and loyalty at instant speed) is 0.614. A combat trick with Empower 2, such as Academic Ascent, stays a trick (0.556).
+
+**Jace token payoffs.** Sanctum Lurker stops the token dying at 0 loyalty and gives it a ping. That is a real engine and a fragile 3/2, rated 0.608 rather than as a mythic. The ten Way enchantments all Empower on entry and staple an activated ability onto every walker, including the token. The cheap ones with a live ability (Cryomancer’s spell copy, Pyromancer’s red mana, Mentor’s lifegain loyalty) are 0.576–0.590. The five-mana ones are lower.
+
+**Removal.** Efficient removal is the most reliable high-GIH effect in the training slices. Last Gasp 0.577, Multiply by Zero (base power and toughness 0/0) 0.586, Fulminous Forte 0.594, the five charms 0.572–0.596. Color-hate removal and counters are maindeck-dead in two or three of the five colleges: Precise Redaction 0.516, Terminal Criticism 0.544, Essence Burn 0.548. Refute Destiny hits green or blue, which is most of the format, so it is not sideboard-only (0.554).
+
+**Prepare.** Rated from the SOS spell, not from the creature’s rarity. Seed Suture (+1/+1 and gain 1) stays near Adventurous Eater. Peer Review and Soul Tether are fine and not exciting. Omit Variables is good only because Theorix wants the mill. Paradox Shaper re-prepares every upkeep and mills three for one mana on a 1/3, which is the best of that cycle (0.570), and it is still not a bomb: the creature has to live. Diviner of Victory is the rare where both halves are good in this format (a one-drop that grows whenever you surveil, and a bounce), 0.606.
+
+**Creatures.** A common two-drop with no text sits near 0.54–0.55. A 2/3 flyer for three (Shatterwing Pegasus) is 0.562. A 3/3 for two mana (Solarium Sentry) is 0.600 because that rate is genuinely ahead of the curve, not because it is rare. Yargle, Glutton of Urborg is a 9/3 for five that dies to the format’s common 3-damage and −3/−3 removal, so 0.570 rather than a 0.62 bomb. The blue 3/9 vanilla is a five-mana wall (0.522). Samut, Hazoret’s Champion gives every creature haste on a two-mana 2/2 (0.616).
+
+**Lands.** Deserted Beach, Haunted Ridge, Overgrown Farmland, Rockfall Vale, and Shipwreck Marsh are exactly the five allied pairs and are the SOS slow lands, so they get that set’s rate (0.574). Theorist’s Sanctum is an Island that enters untapped once you have a Jace and spends mana to Empower (0.582). Roiling Canopy is a tapped Forest with a six-Forest pump (0.505). Hall of Echoes taps for colorless (0.540). Karn, Gilded Guardian costs ten and five colors (0.462). Emrakul’s channel does not reduce its cost; it is a ten-drop people will keep in hand (0.498).
+
+**The top of the set.** The Theorist, Jace Beleren draws an extra card on every opponent’s draw step in a duel, on a four-mana walker that also makes a body and bounces. That is the Ugin/Elspeth tier (0.656), not the median mythic. Kwia Vigorbloom is a 6/6 flying lifelink that makes a Lotus whenever you gain life (0.642). Chandra, Torch of Defiance is the known four-mana walker with mana, impulse, and removal (0.632). Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes is a two-drop whose landfall Empower 2 turns land drops into a draw engine (0.630).
+
+## What this will get wrong
+
+GIH is not card quality in a vacuum. It is the win rate of the decks that draw the card. If a college is much stronger or weaker than the allied-pair read above, every card in that color moves together and these rates will miss by about a point. If prepare plays more like Adventure than it did in Secrets of Strixhaven, the prepare commons are low. If players refuse to play the ten-drops, those GIH samples will be tiny and noisier than a point estimate can capture. The bonus-sheet legends (collector numbers 195–280) are rated as draft cards; if they are opened much less often, their GIH still means the same thing but the sample will be smaller.

+++ b//opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md
@@ -1,0 +1,8 @@
+<decision>
+Predicted one GIH rate per unique Reality Fracture card by measuring Premier Draft game-in-hand rates on the ten historical sets, fitting a gradient-boosted prior, then replacing that prior with card-level rates anchored to realized analogues (SOS prepare, slow lands, Last Gasp, Lightning Strike, Banishing Light) and to the Jace loyalty rules. A pure model was set aside because leave-one-set-out error was 2.6 points and the tree could not price Empower or unique bombs. A flat rarity heuristic was set aside because commons and mythics inside this set span more than 10 points.
+
+<risk>
+The biggest miss is a college being much stronger or weaker than the allied-pair read, which would shift every card in that color together. Prepare is priced off Secrets of Strixhaven; if the mechanic plays closer to Adventure here, those creatures are low. Bonus-sheet legends are rated as if they appear in the draft.
+
+<verified>
+Recomputed GIH from the Premier Draft logs (OM1 Pick-Two). Leave-one-set-out MAE 0.0257. Confirmed the 285 names match the deduped Scryfall file. Checked the published distribution against well-sampled historical GIH (mean, std, p05, p95, rarity medians).
